_why: Every mutation receipt pins the WHOLE-FILE sha256 of five runner components. That
makes any edit to the runner -- a comment, a docstring, a new function -- void every
receipt in the repository at once. Measured 2026-08-30: appending one comment line to
conductor/mutation_testing.py dropped coverage from 505 to 74, with 431 test paths
rejected for 'runner hash mismatch, runner component hash map mismatch'.
That is the same over-broad-pin pathology the per-symbol source pins exist to fix,
one level up: a content pin over an entire file where only a narrow semantic surface
determines what a receipt MEANS.
This file narrows it. An entry declares that receipts produced by the runner at the
recorded hashes are semantically equivalent to receipts produced by the current
runner, because the diff between them does not change how any mutant is applied,
how any outcome is decided, or what any receipt field means.
This is NOT a bypass and NOT the frozen legacy v2 git anchor, which stays frozen:
- it rewrites no receipt -- the 'refuses to write a receipt it did not regenerate'
rule is untouched;
- every entry names its justification and the exact diff it covers;
- deleting an entry restores strict whole-file behaviour immediately;
- an entry is only added after a SAMPLE of campaigns has been re-run under both
runners and shown to produce identical outcomes. Proven, never asserted.
Do NOT add an entry for a change that alters mutant application, outcome
classification, receipt field semantics, or scope validation. Those receipts are
genuinely stale and must be regenerated by re-running their campaigns.

entries.covers_diff: conductor/mutation_testing.py: _run_campaign_command's value-analysis guard no longer refuses every non-pytest batch -- a ctest or cargo batch whose ranked tests are attributable now satisfies it, because analyze_test_value reads report['tests'][nodeid]['outcome'], the same shape the ctest and cargo collectors already emit; and a new _require_declared_adapter binds value_analysis.adapter to the collector actually chosen by nodeid shape, so the label cannot be decorative. conductor/mutation_value.py: two new constants, CTEST_ADAPTER and CARGO_ADAPTER; no behaviour. tooling/native/conductor-native/src/mutation_manifest.rs: the manifest adapter check accepts 'ctest-junit' and 'cargo-libtest' beside 'pytest-junit' -- strictly widening, every previously valid manifest stays valid. No other runner component changed: mutation_campaign_model.py, mutation_patch_apply.py, mutation_receipt_build.py, mutation_scope.py, mutation_testing_support.py, snapshot_worktree.py, mutation_evidence.rs and mutation_receipt.rs are byte-identical to fc990e5bf.
entries.justification: Runner state immediately before value analysis was made reachable for cargo and ctest campaigns. Before this change value analysis was structurally pytest-only through two independent refusals, so no Rust, C or C++ test could ever be classified CORE, MERGE or DELETE_CANDIDATE. The change is strictly widening: it admits batches that were previously REFUSED and therefore produced no receipt at all. For every input that already produced a receipt the code path is unchanged, so it does not alter how a mutant is applied, how an outcome is classified, what any receipt field means, or how a test scope is validated. Receipts produced at these hashes remain exactly as meaningful as ones produced after. The one way this change can newly REFUSE is the adapter-label check, which rejects a manifest whose declared value_analysis.adapter names a harness it will not run under; that was measured against the whole corpus before this entry was written and refuses nothing that exists -- all 180 campaigns carrying value_analysis declare 'pytest-junit' and rank Python nodeids, which is what the pytest collector produces.

The pairs, exactly: mutation_evidence_gate_coverage_20260827_20260906T141628Z.json vs mutation_evidence_gate_coverage_20260827_20260906T143829Z.json (4 mutants, test_value PASS, CORE 4); claude_handoff_module_20260827_20260906T033028Z.json (6 mutants); claude_policy_exceptions_20260906_20260906T125223Z.json (8 mutants); and conductor_graph_context_20260826_20260906T122955Z.json (4 mutants) -- the last three each re-run under the new runner to research/tmp/lineage_proof/<campaign>.new.json, which is scratch and deliberately not committed, since the point is the comparison and not a second receipt. Three of the four carry value_analysis, so conductor/mutation_value.py is exercised on both sides. Separately, the widening itself was proven positive rather than merely harmless: claude_rust_surface_inventory_20260906, a cargo-libtest campaign that the old runner refused outright, now returns PASS with mutation_score 1.0, 10 of 10 mutants killed and 7 of 7 ranked tests classified CORE -- the first cargo campaign in this repository to carry value evidence at all. Control experiment, so the acceptance is attributable to this entry and not to something else in the tree: with this entry removed and nothing else changed, mutation coverage reports 621 of 1236 test files missing; with it present, 604 of 1236. The entry therefore rescues 17 test files and nothing else does, and removing it fails closed immediately.

entries.covers_diff: tooling/native/conductor-native/src/mutation_manifest.rs: CampaignContract gains generated, survivor_baseline and test_sha256 (all #[serde(default)], so an override deserialised from Python still loads); a covers_test method moves the source_sha256-plus-ranked_test_paths test out of the caller; GENERATED_ENGINES, digest_map and generated_campaign_contract are new, and load_campaign_contract returns through the new branch before reading expected_mutations when the manifest declares a generated engine. tooling/native/conductor-native/src/mutation_receipt.rs: runner_errors is extracted from receipt_errors unchanged; generated_receipt_errors is new; receipt_errors returns through it when campaign.generated. tooling/native/conductor-native/src/mutation_evidence.rs: the inline campaign filter is replaced by campaign.covers_test(test_path), which is the same expression for a patch-based contract.
entries.justification: Runner state immediately before the evidence gate learned to accept campaigns whose mutants come from an engine rather than from a committed patch list. Until this change load_campaign_contract had exactly one schema: it required expected_mutations, ranked_tests, planned_mutations and a per-mutant patch digest, so a fest, cargo-mutants or mull manifest could not be registered at all, and receipt_errors required mutation_score == 1.0 with a KILLED outcome for every named mutant. Those two rules together are why 482 of the 483 scored campaigns in this repository publish exactly 1.0: nothing else could land, and the only way to reach 1.0 is to choose the mutants. The change adds a second acceptance rule beside the first rather than altering it. generated_campaign_contract is reached only when mutation_engine names a generated engine, generated_receipt_errors only when the contract it is given came from that branch, and a patch campaign takes neither. The one edit inside the existing path is a pure extraction: the runner component and lineage check was lifted verbatim into runner_errors and is now called from both rules, with the same comparisons in the same order. Receipts produced at the hashes recorded here therefore mean exactly what they meant when they were written.
entries.verified_by: Measured, not asserted. Two patch-based campaigns that carry the hashes recorded here were re-run under the new runner and compared against their existing receipts, matched by manifest_sha256 so the comparison is against the same manifest: mutation_evidence_gate_coverage_20260827, which mutates the evidence gate itself and is the campaign most exposed to this change, and claude_rank8_local_ai_policy_20260830, which carries a non-trivial value-analysis block (CORE 5, DELETE_CANDIDATE 3, INTENTIONAL_REDUNDANCY 2). Both reproduced identically: same status PASS, same mutation_score 1.0, the same outcome for every mutant id, the same killer set for every mutant, and the same test_value classification counts. A third, codex_duplicate_bodies_native_20260903, refused at inspect with source_hash_drift=1 before any mutant ran; that drift predates this change and is unrelated to it.

entries.covers_diff: conductor/mutation_testing.py: _admit_run gains two refusals, both raised ahead of every existing gate in the function -- before a snapshot exists and before any receipt is opened. A campaign declaring one of the generated engines (fest, cargo-mutants, mull) is refused and pointed at `python -m conductor.mutation_engine_generated run`; a campaign carrying no materialized mutations is refused outright. The engine list is read from ADAPTER_MODULES rather than restated, so the refusal cannot drift from the adapter table. The two messages live in conductor/mutation_testing_support.vacuous_run_reason, which takes the engine set as an argument so the support module stays free of conductor imports; mutation_testing.py holds only the call and the raise. Of the eleven paths in RUNNER_COMPONENT_PATHS, exactly those two moved.
entries.justification: Neither new branch is reachable from any receipt this repository holds, and that is a measurement rather than an argument. A receipt is opened only after _admit_run returns, so a run these gates would have refused writes no receipt at all; the question is therefore whether any recorded receipt came from a run that would now be refused. All 676 receipts carrying a runner-component map were read. Six name a generated engine, and every one of the six carries mutants_are_generated: true -- they were written by conductor/mutation_engine_generated.py, which this diff does not touch, and never by the reviewed runner the new gate guards. Four carry zero mutant records, and every one of the four declares a non-empty selected_mutations (34, 1, 6 and 6) with status ERROR or BASELINE_FAILED: their campaigns had materialized mutations and failed later in the run, so campaign.mutations was non-empty and the second gate would not have fired either. Zero receipts sit on either new branch. The entry is needed only because runner components are pinned whole-file, so a 20-line change to one of eleven files stales every receipt at once.
entries.verified_by: The defect was reproduced before and after. Running conductor/mutation_campaigns/claude_mutation_engine_fest_20260906.json through `python -m conductor.mutation_testing run --allow-mutations` on the parent commit loaded the manifest, selected the empty mutation tuple and reported status PASS with mutants 0, selected_mutations [], expected_campaign_mutations 0 and test_value null -- a receipt asserting a campaign passed without a mutant having been applied. The same command on this commit returns status REFUSED naming the engine and the correct entry point, and writes nothing. conductor/test_mutation_testing.py::test_run_requires_explicit_mutation_authority_before_creating_snapshot pins it: the missing authority, then the engine refusal driven from ADAPTER_MODULES so the two cannot drift, asserting the absence of a receipt file for every engine in the table, then the zero-mutation refusal with its planned-count detail. It fails against the parent commit and passes here; the file's other 29 test functions are unchanged and still pass. Six tests over killer attribution and receipt folding moved unmodified into conductor/test_mutation_attribution_verdicts.py so neither module carries the whole framework, and the campaign's complete scope now names both files. mutation_framework_self_v10 was re-pinned and re-run with `repin --run --allow-mutations` rather than hand-edited, so its manifest hashes and its receipt were both regenerated by the tool.
